description: Precision cases for reviews of form fragments. The agent receives only the code and a neutral review request; judge responses against can_conclude / cannot_conclude / must_not by meaning, not by keywords.
request_template: Revisa la accesibilidad (WCAG 2.2 AA) del fragmento que está en {file}. No modifiques ningún archivo. Responde en español.

cases.name: icon_button_without_accessible_name
cases.code:
<button type="button" class="btn-close">
  <svg aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M3 3l10 10M13 3L3 13"/></svg>
</button>
can_conclude: In the supplied markup the button has no accessible name: no text content, aria-label, aria-labelledby or title, and the only child is hidden from AT.
This is a demonstrated issue against 4.1.2 (failure F68); it also leaves a control without a name for speech-input users.
cannot_conclude: What a given screen reader announces (not run).
That CSS-generated content or script elsewhere does not add a name.
That an automated checker would report it (not run).
must_not: Assert the result of running axe or a screen reader.
Cite 2.4.6 as the reason a name is needed.
design_separate: Visible text or a visible icon label benefits sighted speech-input and cognitive users (2.5.3 applies if visible label text exists).

cases.name: input_without_any_name_source
can_conclude: No <label>, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title or placeholder: the field has no accessible name in the supplied markup (4.1.2, F68).
No label or instruction is provided for input (3.3.2) in this fragment.
cannot_conclude: That the page has no nearby visible text elsewhere that a script associates with it.
That 1.3.5 applies: nothing shows it collects information about the user.
must_not: Claim a screen reader announcement or tool result.
design_separate: A persistent visible <label> is the recommended fix.

cases.name: aria_label_without_label_element
can_conclude: The field has an accessible name through aria-label, so it is not a 4.1.2 failure merely for lacking a <label>.
Whether a label is presented to all users (3.3.2) depends on visible text elsewhere on the page: a visual check; the name may be hidden but the label is for everyone.
cannot_conclude: That the missing <label> element is a failure of 4.1.2, 1.3.1 or 2.4.6.
That 3.3.2 fails or passes from this fragment alone.
must_not: Report the absence of <label> as a certain failure.
Use 2.4.6 as a requirement to create a label.
design_separate: A visible label is recommended; if visible label text exists, include it in the name (2.5.3).

cases.name: placeholder_only_identifier
can_conclude: There is no <label>, aria-label or aria-labelledby; the only identifying text is the placeholder.
Under the HTML-AAM mapping (a Working Draft, not WCAG) the placeholder is a fallback accessible name, so a name probably exists; verify in the browser accessibility tree.
Concerns (text disappears on input, contrast, no persistent label) are real usability risks; whether 3.3.2 is met is a judgement about the page.
cannot_conclude: That the field automatically passes or fails 4.1.2, 1.3.1, 3.3.2 or 2.4.6.
That 1.3.5 applies (an order number is not information about the user from the input-purposes list).
must_not: Declare a definite WCAG failure solely because there is no <label>.
Stack 1.3.1, 2.4.6, 3.3.2 and 4.1.2 without a reason for each.
design_separate: Recommend a persistent visible <label> as a design/usability improvement.

cases.name: label_text_type_with_autocomplete_email
cases.code:
<label for="correo">Correo electrónico</label>
<input id="correo" type="text" name="correo" autocomplete="email">
can_conclude: The field has a label and accessible name.
autocomplete="email" identifies the input purpose (H98), so 1.3.5 is met as far as the markup shows, if the field collects the user's email.
type="text" is not by itself a 1.3.5 failure.
cannot_conclude: That type="text" is a failure of any criterion.
Anything about validation behavior or server handling.
design_separate: type="email" is a usability suggestion (mobile keyboard, native validation), distinct from autocomplete.

cases.name: fragment_without_required_or_server_info
cases.code:
<form action="/suscribir" method="post">
  <label for="correo">Correo electrónico</label>
  <input id="correo" type="email" name="correo" autocomplete="email">
  <button type="submit">Suscribirme</button>
</form>
can_conclude: The supplied markup shows no problem with names, labels or input purpose.
Whether the field is required, what errors appear and how the server responds are not visible in the fragment.
cannot_conclude: That required-field information is missing (3.3.2) or that error identification, suggestions or status messages (3.3.1, 3.3.3, 4.1.3) fail.
must_not: Present the absence of `required` or of error markup as a failure.
Assign severity to things not shown.
design_separate: Optional: mention checking error handling and status announcements in the real page.
